title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Optimized Wrench Polytope for Real-Time Legged Stability

### The Breakthrough
The authors present a fast algorithm that computes the full actuatable wrench polytope for arbitrary contact configurations at 49 Hz, enabling per‑joint torque computation within the main control loop. This speed allows on‑the‑fly torque calculation and yields stable locomotion on a physical legged robot in complex multi‑contact scenarios previously unattainable.

### The Caveats
The paper shows stable locomotion but offers no quantitative comparison to existing controllers, leaving the claimed real‑time advantage unsubstantiated.

## Agility Robotics Digit 5 Safety Motion

### The Breakthrough
Agility Robotics unveiled Digit 5, equipped with a complex safe motion system that classifies human proximity and instantly halts, sidesteps, or assumes a squatted posture, extending safety beyond simple stop‑and‑wait behaviors. Early access is slated for the first half of 2027.

### The Caveats
No empirical safety performance data or real‑world trials are provided, so the claim of safe collaborative operation remains unsubstantiated.

## UBTECH 10k‑Unit Humanoid Smart Factory

### The Breakthrough
UBTECH opened a 14,000 m² smart factory that can assemble an industrial humanoid robot every 10 minutes, using a Siemens‑co‑developed manufacturing operations platform, simulation‑driven scheduling, and automated stereoscopic warehousing that stores 112 robots in 65 m².

### The Caveats
The claimed 10‑minute‑per‑unit throughput and 10 k‑unit annual capacity are unverified, with no independent performance data.

## Waymo Tokyo Robotaxi Service 2027

### The Breakthrough
Waymo plans to launch a fully driverless robotaxi fleet in Tokyo by 2027, integrating its proven self‑driving stack with local taxi partners to operate up to 100 vehicles without safety drivers.

### The Caveats
The announcement lacks independent verification, regulatory approvals, or performance data.

## Tesla Cybercab FMVSS Compliance Order

### The Breakthrough
Tesla introduced a steering‑wheel‑free Cybercab that it self‑certified as meeting all applicable FMVSS, marking the first commercial robotaxi without traditional driver controls; NHTSA now demands proof of compliance under oath.

### The Caveats
Tesla’s compliance claim is unsubstantiated, with no independent safety validation.

## Online Geometric Change Detection via Scene Decomposition (CDSD)

### The Breakthrough
The CDSD framework breaks dense SLAM maps into local submaps, allowing online geometric change detection using LiDAR or RGB‑D sensors with reduced computational load while maintaining accuracy, demonstrated on custom ARL facility data and public multi‑session datasets.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no quantitative comparison to existing change‑detection baselines.

## Motion‑Prior Regularization for Data‑Scarce Insertion

### The Breakthrough
By adding minimum‑jerk and speed‑curvature priors to diffusion‑policy training on just 15 demonstrations, the method achieved up to 87.5% success on a peg‑in‑hole insertion task across 80 real‑robot trials, showing simple priors can mitigate data scarcity.

### The Caveats
Results are confined to a single insertion task on one robot, so generalization remains unclear.

## Modality‑Autoregressive World‑Action Models (ModAR)

### The Breakthrough
ModAR autoregressively denoises multiple future visual modalities before predicting actions, reaching 75% success on three real‑world bimanual manipulation tasks while using ~20× fewer FLOPs and no pretraining compared to prior models.

### The Caveats
The paper never ablates the contribution of each generated modality, leaving the source of success gains uncertain.

### Priority
The legged‑robot stability breakthrough offers a real‑time, hardware‑validated controller that immediately expands the capabilities of versatile legged platforms.

### One action
Explore integrating the open‑source wrench‑polytope code into your legged robot stack or benchmark against its 49 Hz performance.

### What to watch
Both the motion‑prior regularization work and ModAR aim to improve data‑efficient manipulation. The former leverages simple kinematic priors on a diffusion policy for a single insertion task, while the latter builds a multimodal world‑action model that predicts richer visual cues before actions across multiple bimanual tasks. Future research may combine these approaches, using priors to guide multimodal autoregressive predictions for broader, low‑data manipulation challenges.
